title: Embeddings & Reranking - Performance & Cost deep dive
summary: Deep dive on embeddings/reranking tradeoffs: vector dimensionality, batching, latency SLOs, KV cache usage, quantization impact, and VPC/on-prem constraints. We aligned on benchmark plan (dims: 128/256/512, batch sizes: 1/8/32/128), agreed target p95/p99 SLOs, and next steps: pricing, security docs, and pilot benchmarking week.
topics: Batch sizes and GPU throughput vs tail latency
KV cache behavior and when to use it for reranking
Quantization (int8/4-bit) impact on recall and speed
VPC / on-prem deployment considerations and network hop latency
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Jasmine (Solutions Eng), Alex (VectorFin CTO), Priya (ML Eng), Michael (Infra), Sofia (Product)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we scheduled this as a technical deep dive on your embeddings + reranking flow, just to make sure we understand latency and cost constraints, so quick intro?
[00:12] Alex: yeah thanks, i'm alex, CTO at vectorfin, we run a realtime recommendation pipeline - low latency is critical, target 99th under 150ms if possible.
[00:22] Priya: hi all, priya here, owning the model infra and the evals, our current infra is a managed vector db and single-node GPU for embed calc, but we're hitting latency at scale.
[00:31] Miguel: great, quick Q: are you doing separate embed generation at query time or precomputed?
[00:36] Priya: precomputed for corpus, but query-side we compute embedding for the query and do ANN search then rerank top-k with a small cross-encoder reranker.
[00:44] Jasmine: and what's your current vector dim and index type?
[00:47] Priya: 768 dims, faiss IVF HNSW hybrid, but we're experimenting with 512 and 256 to see perf tradeoffs.
[00:54] Samira: ok that's helpful; main things we'll cover: dim tradeoffs, batch sizing for embed generation and reranker, how KV cache interacts, and quantization options for the reranker and embed model.

[01:20] Miguel: first data point - raw embedding compute latency roughly scales linearly with dim and model flops; on a single A10/A100 a 768-d model at batch=1 is often 20-50ms depending on model and optimizations; dropping to 256d can drop that to ~8-18ms. but throughput improves significantly with batching.
[01:45] Priya: can you clarify those numbers? we measured ~70ms p95 for our query embed compute on a shared gpu; is that expected?
[01:52] Miguel: yeah if shared GPU and no KV cache and you have context switching, p95 can spike. Dedicated and proper batching brings that down. Also quantization helps memory footprint so more concurrency.

[02:20] Alex: reranker is our biggest cost; we're running cross-encoder on top-32 candidates, and that multiplies compute. We tried batch 1 sequentially and it's too slow.
[02:31] Jasmine: common pattern is to run the embed-ANN to get top-N (say 200), then cheap lexical or dot-prod score to narrow to 32, then cross-encoder rerank. If the reranker accepts batched inputs you can amortize per-request cost by batching multiple queries or doing micro-batching.
[02:45] Michael: but micro-batching adds latency. we need to understand the sweet spot between throughput/cost and our 99th target.

[03:10] Miguel: right - example tradeoff: cross-encoder single-example latency 30ms p50, 90ms p95 on A10 quantized; with batch=8 you might get amortized per-item latency of ~12-20ms but tail can increase unless you use continuous batching inside the runtime. our runtime supports adaptive batching with SLO profiles.
[03:35] Priya: when you say quantized, you mean int8 or 4-bit? impact on accuracy?
[03:39] Miguel: both are viable; int8 usually yields minimal recall drop (~0-1% in our evals), 4-bit/LLM-int4 can be model-dependent and sometimes a 1-3% drop. we recommend running A/B on your reranker thresholds (recall@K).

[04:05] Alex: ok and KV cache - we mostly associated that with generation caching. does KV cache help reranking/embeddings?
[04:12] Samira: good question - KV cache is primarily for autoregressive decoders; for embeddings/rerank the equivalent is caching computed query embeddings or ANN results. Redwood supports prefix caching and application-level caching hooks. so for repeated queries you can short-circuit embed compute. but for unique queries caching helps less.
[04:34] Priya: we have a fair bit of repeated queries for common instruments, so caching could save ops. what's the storage tradeoff?
[04:40] Miguel: storing 512-d floats for million keys is ~2GB per million entries at float32? to calc: 512 dims * 4 bytes = ~2KB per vector, wait math: 512*4=2048 bytes, so ~2KB -> 1M vectors = ~2GB. If you quantize to float16 or use PQ/storage formats, storage drops a lot. many customers use product quantization in their ANN store to reduce memory and then keep hot vectors in memory cache.
[05:08] Alex: interesting, so vector dim reduction plus quantization both reduce memory and inference cost, but we need to see effect on rerank recall.

[05:20] Priya: benchmark plan? we need to test dims [128,256,512], batch sizes [1,8,32,128], and measure p50/p95/p99 for embed compute and reranker for top-32. Also recall@1/5/10 deltas.
[05:33] Samira: that's exactly what we recommend. our suggested benchmark matrix: for each dim (128/256/512) run queries at qps levels {10,50,200} with batch-sweeps on both embed compute and reranker; measure latency distribution, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k requests. we'll also test quantized model variants (int8 and 4-bit) for the reranker.

[06:00] Miguel: small note on batch sizes: embedding gen is embarrassingly parallel and benefits more from large batches (e.g., batch 32/128) on GPU, but query latency suffers for synchronous real-time. reranker benefits most from batching multiple requests or using a streaming reranker with early-stopping heuristics.
[06:22] Sofia: for product, the user experience expects sub-100ms in the UI, can we hit p95 under 100 with reranker included?
[06:29] Miguel: it's possible with dedicated capacity, smaller dims, and batching plus caching; e.g., 256d embed + optimized ANN + quantized reranker on dedicated A100-like infra often gets p95 ~70-120ms for top-32 rerank depending on model complexity. but need to validate with your model weights.

[07:00] Alex: network hops for VPC/on-prem matter too. our infra sits in GCP with private peering; what network overhead do you see with Redwood Private?
[07:08] Samira: with Redwood Private in VPC mode typical network overhead is single-digit ms if colocated regionally; on-prem with a VPN can add 10-40ms depending on topology. we also support customer-hosted runtimes if you need zero egress for embeddings.
[07:26] Michael: good, we have compliance constraints
d encrypt at rest and KMS integration required.
[07:30] Samira: we will share SOC2 and KMS integration docs. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and audit logs; we'll include those in the security pack.

[08:00] Priya: any gotchas with quantized rerankers in production? e.g., non-determinism or increased tail latency?
[08:06] Miguel: quantized kernels can increase jitter if kernel fusion isn't optimized for your sequence lengths; also some older drivers have slower int8 paths. our runtime chooses kernels based on observed latencies; we recommend testing on your target hardware.

[09:00] Jasmine: on the runtime side, we also have continuous batching which tries to hold requests for a configurable max latency budget (e.g., 10ms) to accumulate a batch. that reduces cost while bounding added latency. customers pick SLO targets that drive the batching policy.

[09:30] Alex: so if we set SLO p95=100ms, runtime will microbatch up to a configured wait cap and then dispatch?
[09:36] Miguel: exactly - you set a latency cap (max wait) and a batch cap; runtime balances throughput and SLOs. for very tight p99 it's common to use dedicated non-shared capacity and lower batch caps.

[10:05] Priya: about ANN search - does Redwood manage indices or do we keep our vector db?
[10:10] Samira: you can bring your own ANN/db; many customers use managed vector DBs like we discussed (pinecone, milvus), or we can host the ANN close to the inference to reduce network hops. for highest perf we colocate ANN and reranker in same VPC/host.

[10:45] Alex: competitors - pinecone and milvus mentioned earlier as vector stores, openai for managed embeddings. we want a single vendor if possible but open to hybrid.

[11:00] Miguel: ok let's walk through a concrete sample: suppose you target 100ms p95 total. Option A: 512d embed (precomputed) + ANN for top-200 + quantized cross-encoder rerank on dedicated GPU with batch=8 continuous batching. Cost: higher than 256d but better recall. Option B: move to 256d and int8 reranker, reduces compute and memory by ~30-50% with small recall hits.

[12:10] Priya: can you give ballpark cost numbers for dedicated per-1k requests?
[12:14] Samira: ballpark for embedded + rerank on dedicated infra depends on model sizes; rough example: dedicated capacity amortized cost (infra + license) could be $0.20-$1.20 per 1k requests depending on batch efficiency and model. hosted optimized flows when batched heavily can be cheaper but less isolated. we'll send a cost spreadsheet with your actual qps numbers.

[12:40] Alex: need precise numbers to justify infra spend to finance.
[12:43] Samira: understood; we'll run the benchmark with your traces and return a per-scenario cost calc.

[13:10] Miguel: on metrics to collect during benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latency for embed and rerank, GPU util, memory pressure, effective batch sizes, recall@1/5/10, index search recall, and cost per 1k. Also track tail latency sources (queueing vs kernel).

[14:00] Priya: dataset for benchmark - we can share a 10k query trace and a 1M corpus subset.

[15:00] Alex: curious about on-prem - if we run the runtime ourselves, do we lose Redwood Optimize suggestions?
[15:06] Jasmine: no, Private deployment includes the same Optimize toolkit; some telemetry is optional—can run with limited telemetry for compliance. you still get batching/caching/quantization recommendations locally.

[15:40] Michael: provisioning test VPC - what's the access model? we prefer temporary service account + IP allowlist.

[16:10] Priya: one operational question: how do we handle versioning of reranker models for rollouts?
[16:15] Miguel: Redwood supports pinned model versions, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to previous model versions if quality or latency regresses. rollouts can be traffic-weighted and tied to evals/prompt test sets.

[16:45] Sofia: what's the expected timeline for a pilot?

[17:14] Samira: recap and next steps at the end, but before that any final clarifying q's?

[18:20] Samira: RECAP - agree benchmark matrix (dims: 128/256/512; batch sweep: 1/8/32/128; qps targets 10/50/200), run quantized variants (int8 & 4-bit) of the reranker, test caching strategies for repeated queries, measure p50/p95/p99 and recall@K, and provide cost-per-1k scenarios and recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

[19:05] Alex: will upload traces and a sample corpus by end of week.
